artifact.version_note: Official PMLR published version, 34 PDF pages corresponding to proceedings pp. 135–168; title and all seven ordered authors read on first page.

contexts.evidence: Sections 3.3–3.4 develop transformer-specific relevance rules; the related-work classification is accurate.
Sections 3.2–3.4 cover linear operations, attention and normalization; this is a transformer LRP method.
Section 3.3, pp. 5–6, derives softmax and bilinear-product propagation rather than freezing the attention matrix.
Section 3.3 gives dedicated rules; Section 4 evaluates LLaMa 2, Mixtral, Flan-T5 and ViTs.
Appendix A.2.2, p. 16, explicitly describes CP-LRP treating attention probabilities as constant and attributing only Values.
Section 3.3 and Appendix A.2.2 distinguish AttnLRP propagation through attention-generating operations from CP-LRP.
Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2 confirm that AttnLRP propagates through softmax and the bilinear products.
The abstract links the authors' LXT implementation; Appendix B.5/Table B.5 specify the ViT composite.
Section 4.1 evaluates AttnLRP on ViTs, supporting baseline identity; reported new numerical comparisons belong to the thesis.
Section 3.3 defines relevance propagation through softmax, Query/Key products and the Value product.
Table B.5, p. 25, confirms gamma values 0.25/0.05 and epsilon projection rules; LXT linear_epsilon defaults to 1e-6.

notes: The existing full author name is correct, but the publisher and official implementation BibTeX parse the second author as Hatefi, Sayed Mohammad Vakilzadeh, rather than Vakilzadeh Hatefi, Sayed Mohammad. Proposed entry follows that authoritative name parsing.

The fixed-attention sentence in chapter 7 line 75 is supported by this paper's discussion of CP-LRP, not by AttnLRP's own propagation rules. The surrounding thesis correctly distinguishes these methods.
Citations identifying an experimental baseline are supported; this source cannot independently validate the thesis's own experimental comparisons or implementation choices.

Table B.5 gives convolution gamma 0.25, other-linear gamma 0.05, and epsilon rules for attention input/output projections. It does not specify the numerical epsilon value. The declared epsilon_attn = 1e-6 is consistent with the default linear_epsilon in the official LXT source; attention matrix multiplication defaults have varied, so the thesis implementation remains the authority for this parameter.

metadata_sources.supports: Canonical ICLR record identifier; browser challenge prevented direct page retrieval.
Author-affiliated publication list confirms title, ordered author identities and ICLR 2018.
Exact ordered author list, title and preprint identifier/version.

artifact.version_note: arXiv:1705.05598v2 dated 24 October 2017; title and all seven ordered authors verified. OpenReview PDF download returned HTTP 403, so content was read from the corresponding author-deposited preprint. Google Research and author-affiliated institutional records confirm ICLR 2018.

contexts.evidence: Section 2, pp. 3–4, shows that the learned filter/gradient direction follows input distractors and need not identify the signal; this supports the broad concern about input dependence.
Section 2 and Figure 2 demonstrate distractor-driven gradients; Sections 3–4 distinguish signal attribution from function visualization and learn signal patterns from input statistics.

notes: The input-dependence wording is supportable when read as dependence on input signal/distractor statistics: Section 2 demonstrates that gradients can follow distractor directions. This paper is not the separate Kindermans input-invariance paper, so stronger claims about invariance to constant input shifts would require that different source.
Google Research's web page misspells Klaus-Robert as Klaus-Robet; the full paper and arXiv author record confirm Klaus-Robert, already correct in the thesis.

verified_metadata.title: A Simple Sequentially Rejective Multiple Test Procedure

metadata_sources.supports: Actual journal scan: title, author, journal, volume 6, year 1979, pages 65–70; University of Granada institutional copy.
National library catalogue confirms author, title, journal, year, volume and pages.
Stable archive identifier; direct archive access was limited in this environment.

artifact.version_note: Six-page scan of the published 1979 article. pdftotext produced only page breaks because this is an image PDF; title/authors and pp. 65–67 were verified visually from rendered pages saved alongside the PDF.

contexts.evidence: Section 2, pp. 66–67, gives the sequentially rejective Bonferroni procedure, and Theorem 1 proves familywise significance control. It is applicable to a family of valid paired-test p-values; the paper does not itself establish the thesis-specific experimental implementation.

Section 2, Scheme 1 and Theorem 1 (p. 67) apply the step-down thresholds to the ordered p-values of a defined family. This supports correcting all pairwise comparisons before selecting reported comparisons. Section 1 (p. 65) also distinguishes rejection guarantees from acceptance of a null hypothesis.

notes: The supplied bibliographic facts were correct but encoded as misc with the journal in note; normalize to article with journal/volume/number/pages fields.
Do not add the frequently repeated pseudo-DOI 10.2307/4615733 without further verification: both DOI resolution and Crossref lookup returned 404 during this audit. The JSTOR stable URL is sufficient.
Citation support was checked against the actual scanned article, not merely a secondary explanation of Holm correction.

metadata_sources.supports: Publisher confirms exact title, V. A. Zalgaller, journal, volume 100, pp. 2209–2227, June 2000, DOI, and translation provenance.
Original journal record links the 1997 Russian original to the English translation in Journal of Mathematical Sciences 100(3), 2209–2227 (2000).

artifact.version_note: Publisher PDF of the English journal translation, 19 pages, Journal of Mathematical Sciences 100(3), 2000. Title, V. A. Zalgaller, pagination and translation provenance match. Extracted text saved as papers/Zalgaller2000_DCRepresentation.txt.

contexts.evidence: Section 4.1–4.2, pp. 2211–2212, defines continuous piecewise-linear functions on a compact convex polytope and proves they can be expressed as differences of two convex piecewise-linear functions in arbitrary dimension. This directly supports the cited DC-existence background. The restriction to dimensions 1 and 2 in the abstract concerns finite algorithms for minimal representations, not Theorem 4.2's existence statement.

notes: The supplied metadata is correct. Issue 3 is verified and may optionally be added as number = {3}; omission is not an error.
The 2000 article is the English translation of the 1997 Russian paper; the downloaded English publication agrees with the bibliography year.
